findings.evidence: http://HOST/ (HTTP 200) serves only 547 characters (72 words) of extractable body text; the element #dynamic-section is empty in the raw HTML and is populated at runtime by inline JavaScript carrying 97 characters of markup (8 words) across 1 injection sites. Facts visible only after JS execution include the prices "$0.023, $399".

suggested_action.mechanism: Most AI retrieval pipelines index the raw HTTP response; content injected by the browser after load is invisible to them, so JS-only facts are simply absent from the model's evidence.
suggested_action.summary: Server-side render (SSR) or statically pre-render the product, pricing and company sections into the initial HTML response for #dynamic-section inside <main>, keeping JavaScript for enhancement only, and mirror the same values in Product/Offer JSON-LD structured data. Verify with a text-only fetch (`curl`) that the raw HTML already carries the prices, so the facts are machine-readable for AI crawlers and assistants that never execute JavaScript and can be extracted and cited.

findings.evidence: Scanned 547 characters of extractable text across 1 crawled pages from http://HOST/ (HTTP 200): 3 spellings of the same organisation occupy the identity slots: "CloudPeak Technologies" (h1, title); "Cloud Peak Tech" (body 'Welcome to'); "CP Technologies" ('About' heading). "CloudPeak Technologies" and "CP Technologies" are 80% string-similar, i.e. variants of one another rather than separate companies, and 2 such near-duplicate pairs were measured in total.

suggested_action.mechanism: Assistants resolve a page to an entity before they cite it. Competing names split the evidence across several weak candidate entities, so the brand is described vaguely, attributed to the wrong name, or dropped from the answer.
suggested_action.summary: Pick one canonical legal name and use it verbatim in the <title>, <h1>, footer copyright and the JSON-LD Organization `name` property on every HTML page, demoting every other spelling to `alternateName` in that same Organization block, and add `sameAs` links to the company's LinkedIn and Crunchbase profiles. One machine-readable name lets AI systems and crawlers resolve every page to a single entity they can trust, extract and cite.

findings.evidence: 0 of 1 crawled pages expose structured data: http://HOST/ (HTTP 200) serves 547 characters (72 words) of organisation, product and contact information in prose but contains 0 application/ld+json blocks and 0 itemtype/typeof attributes.

suggested_action.mechanism: Schema.org markup is the one channel where a site states its own facts unambiguously; without it every extraction is an inference that an assistant may decline to cite.
suggested_action.summary: Add an Organization JSON-LD block in the HTML <head> of every page (name, url, logo, description, address, contactPoint, sameAs) and Product/Offer JSON-LD next to each product section, so the facts that are currently prose-only become machine-readable and AI systems can extract and cite them as attributed entity data instead of inferring them from the copy.

findings.evidence: http://HOST/ (HTTP 200) presents 2 fact-bearing images (2 images across 1 pages) whose alt text is missing or generic, and whose surrounding sections contain fewer than 30 words of prose: customer-results.png (alt="results", under "Our Customers and Results"); partnership-logos.png (alt="partners", under "Our Customers and Results"). The page's own extractable text is 547 characters, so these facts exist nowhere in machine-readable form.

suggested_action.mechanism: Text extractors and LLM retrieval pipelines do not OCR images; a fact that exists only as pixels is invisible to the model even though a human sees it immediately.
suggested_action.summary: Reproduce the content of each image as HTML text next to it - a real <table> for the pricing and feature matrix, a text block for the company infographic, and vCard-style markup for the contact card - then add descriptive alt text (or a <figcaption>) stating the specific facts shown. Mirror the same values in Product/Offer JSON-LD so the numbers are machine-readable and AI systems can extract and cite them from the HTML instead of ignoring the images.

findings.evidence: Across 547 characters of body text, 4 dated claims on http://HOST/ (HTTP 200) reference 2018-2020, i.e. 6+ years before the current year 2026; the spread covers award x2, pricing x1, undated claim x1. Examples: "r of "Best Cloud Startup" at TechSummit 2018. Named a Gartner Cool Ve"; "it 2018. Named a Gartner Cool Vendor in 2019. Industry data: Cloud ma"; "ta: Cloud market worth $250B (Statista, 2019) Contact Email: info@cpe". 1 of 1 crawled pages carry no current-year date at all, and the copyright on them still reads 2020, 6 years stale. No date at or after last year appears anywhere in the crawled text.

suggested_action.mechanism: Recency is a ranking and trust signal for AI answer engines: when the newest date on a page is years old, retrieval systems down-rank it and assistants prefer a competitor's current page, even if your facts are still accurate.
suggested_action.summary: Refresh the dated blocks in priority order - pricing tables first, then statistics, awards, team and press - stamp each with a visible 'Last updated' date plus a machine-readable `dateModified` in the page's JSON-LD, and generate the footer copyright year from the server clock so the HTML never contradicts the content. Label genuinely historical facts as such ('award received in 2019'). Recency that AI systems can extract is what keeps the page eligible to be cited rather than skipped.

findings.evidence: http://HOST/ (HTTP 200) serves 547 characters of content but contains 0 <nav> landmarks, 0 internal links and 0 external links; header/footer/breadcrumb landmarks present: 0 of 3. The same pattern holds on 1 of 1 measurable pages, so every page is a dead end for a visitor who arrives from a search result or an AI citation.

suggested_action.mechanism: Internal links are how crawlers discover pages and how AI systems infer site structure and topical relationships; without them each page is an isolated document, and a visitor who lands mid-site has no path to a conversion step.
suggested_action.summary: Add a persistent header <nav> linking Home, About, Products, Pricing and Contact on every HTML page, a footer with the same site-wide links plus policy pages, and breadcrumbs marked up as machine-readable BreadcrumbList JSON-LD on sub-pages. Cross-link related products and articles in body copy so visitors and AI crawlers can discover, extract and cite the rest of the site from any entry point.
